meta.title: Official booking-engine captures — 7 nights, 2 adults
meta.why: The canonical hotel table uses Booking.com snapshots (F-29). This file records what the properties' OWN booking engines returned for the preferred dates, read directly from the engine on 27 Nov 2026. It is deliberately small and dated: it is a snapshot, not a quotable price.
meta.tax_fee_basis: As printed by each engine. Caesars and Wynn show a nightly rate that INCLUDES the resort fee but EXCLUDES tax. Resorts World shows a full itemised total that includes room tax, resort fee and resort-fee tax.
meta.rule: Only values visible on the engine's own page are recorded, with the exact URL. A blank means the engine did not return a readable result for this session. Nothing is extrapolated from another property or another date.
caveats: These are live engine outputs captured at one moment. Rates move; the same page re-read the next day can differ (F-30).
Caesars displayed a 'technical difficulties' banner while still rendering room rates; the rates are shown but the banner is disclosed.
A 'room type assigned on arrival' rate does not guarantee the bed size the brief requires (F-11). Those rows are marked.

what_this_does_not_establish: It is NOT a market-wide 'cheapest week' answer. Three properties are covered on one date window.
It does NOT prove February is cheaper than March — no March window was re-read on these engines in this pass.
It does NOT reproduce the Booking.com totals in the canonical table; the sources and fee bases differ (F-29/F-44).
It cannot be compared with the Booking.com rows without adding the resort fee and 13.38% room tax to those rows.

window_comparison.question: Is February (the preferred window) actually cheaper than later in the travel window?
window_comparison.method: The SAME room (Deluxe Room - One King Bed, Hilton tower, Resorts World), the SAME booking engine, 7 nights, 2 adults, read in the SAME session on 2026-11-27, changing only the arrival date. Because nothing but the dates varies, the totals are directly comparable to each other.
window_comparison.basis: All totals are all-in: nightly room rates + room tax + $385 resort fees + resort-fee tax, exactly as the engine itemised them.

windows.note: The brief's preferred window. Contains the two most expensive nights of any window sampled ($348.75 on Tue 16 and Wed 17).
Most expensive of the four. Driven by a $399 night on Sun 28 Feb.
Cheapest of the four by a wide margin: four nights at $96.75 or below.
Mid-range. Also inside the brief's travel window (which ends 23 Mar 2027).

window_comparison.what_this_establishes: On this property, on this engine, on 2026-11-27, 8-15 March 2027 cost $1,646.57 all-in against $2,200.15 for the preferred 15-22 February — a $553.58 difference (25.2% less) for an identical room and identical stay length.
what_this_does_not_establish: It is ONE property. It does not show that March is cheaper market-wide; other properties may price differently.
It is ONE capture moment. Rates move daily, and a promotional rate valid today may not exist tomorrow.
It does not prove booking earlier or later will be cheaper — no purchase-timing evidence exists (F-58).
The 8 March window is still inside the brief's 15 Feb - 23 Mar travel window, so this is a within-brief substitution, not a different trip.
It does not account for convention calendars, which can invert the ranking at other properties on the same dates.
